cleanup-mcp-session-scope.test.sh fails identically on origin/main and this branch (fixture: foreign process did not report a pid) — pre-existing, off-CI only, in scope for PR #485.
learnings: Never edit a shell script while a test run is executing it — bash reads scripts incrementally by byte offset, so an in-flight edit shifts offsets and produces a bogus 'syntax error near unexpected token' at an unrelated line. Diagnose by re-running cleanly before believing the error.

Establish a baseline by running the suite against origin/main BEFORE attributing failures to your change; two of the three failures seen in this session were machine-load flake and a pre-existing off-CI fixture failure, not regressions.

When a long-running headless agent replies in prose instead of the requested JSON, the work is usually already done — the reply's envelope (num_turns after compaction) shows it lost the output contract, not the task. Recover the envelope; do not re-run the work.
decisions: Repair pass is a REFORMAT not a retry: no tools, no re-work, prompt forbids inventing an outcome the reply does not state and requires the blocked/failing reading when ambiguous; repaired output is validated against the script's own schema exactly like a first-pass reply, so nothing unvalidated reaches the script.

Resume uses strict prefix semantics matching the Workflow tool: first key mismatch permanently ends the replay for the whole run, because later agent calls consume earlier results and a cached downstream answer would no longer correspond to live state.

Cache key = sha256(engine, tier, model, effort, label, prompt, schema, extraArgs, workDir); checked BEFORE the semaphore so a replayed agent holds no concurrency slot; replayed calls are journalled as normal agent-done with cached:true so resumes chain.

Extracted argv-building + spawn from agent() into runEngine() rather than duplicating flag construction for the repair spawn — three engines' worth of flags is the part most likely to drift if copied. Refactored against the existing 61-check suite as the safety net.

Changed rather than deleted the existing assertion 'schema-violating JSON is rejected with a schema error': it now runs with HQ_WORKFLOW_REPAIR=0, so the guarantee (wrong-shape reply never reaches the script) stays pinned independently of whether a repair pass exists.
